PR body:
  | Supersedes #2160, whose commit is the first one here, rebased onto main with the fixes to it folded in.
  | 
  | go-git did not consult `protocol.allow`, `protocol.<name>.allow`, `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` or `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER`, so a `.gitmodules` entry could make a submodule update fetch over `file://` or any other scheme Git refuses by default. This enforces Git's protocol policy at the transport handshake, as [`transport_check_allowed`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/transport.c#L1037-L1150) does.
  | 
  | ## Changes
  | 
  | - **Policy gate.** `client.Client` and each built-in transport check the request's scheme before handshaking or connecting. Defaults match Git: http, https, git and ssh are `always`, ext is `never`, and file and unknown schemes are `user`. Denial returns `transport.ErrProtocolNotAllowed`. `client.WithProtocolPolicy` and `client.WithUserInitiated` supply the policy inputs.
  | - **Lookup-time validation.** As in Git, an allow value is checked when a transport looks it up, through the new `Config.ProtocolPolicy`, not when the config loads: one bad `[protocol "foo"] allow = bogus` no longer stops `PlainOpen`. An unknown or empty value fails the lookup with Git's "unknown value for config '…'" message. `Protocol.Allow` is a `*string`, nil when unset, so an empty value stays set through marshalling and scope merging.
  | - **Every config scope.** Fetches, pushes and submodule updates read the policy from the repository config merged with the global and system configs when a `ConfigLoader` plugin is registered (the default), as Git reads all three. A global file that cannot be read for lack of permission is skipped, and `~/.gitconfig` then gives way to the XDG file, while an unreadable system file fails the operation, as in [Git](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/config.c#L1541-L1557). Unlike Git, only one global file is read, `~/.gitconfig` or else the XDG one, and `[include]` and `[includeIf]` are not followed.
  | - **Submodules.** Submodule fetches are never user-initiated: `WithUserInitiated(false)` now follows the caller's options, as Git's submodule update sets `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER=0` whatever the caller passes. A caller's `WithProtocolPolicy` still overlays the submodule's policy key by key, like `git -c`.
  | - **Redirects.** Every HTTP redirect hop is checked against the policy as a non-user request, as Git restricts [`CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/http.c#L1148-L1161). This refuses an http to https hop under `protocol.https.allow=never`, and an http to http one under `protocol.http.allow=user`.
  | - **Config round-trips.** Clearing `Protocol.Allow` or a per-scheme entry removes the key on marshal, without dropping `protocol.version`, unrelated keys or the other entries. A config read error fails the operation rather than falling back to the defaults.
  | 
  | ## Behaviour changes
  | 
  | - A `file://` submodule is refused unless `protocol.file.allow` (in any scope) or `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` allows it, as in Git.
  | - A redirect to a protocol the policy forbids for non-user requests fails a handshake that used to follow it.
  | - Fetch, push, `Remote.List` and `ArchiveRemote` now read the host's global and system config on every operation; before, they read no host config at all.
  | - A global or system config with bad syntax now fails them, as it fails Git. A value go-git would refuse elsewhere in those files, such as `[pack] window = x`, does not, since only the protocol policy is interpreted.
  | - The `ConfigLoader` plugin key is frozen at the first such operation, so an embedder must register its loader before it; registering later returns `plugin.ErrFrozen`.
  | - An unreadable global config file (`~/.gitconfig`, the XDG file or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`) is skipped rather than failing the operation, as Git skips it; this also applies to `Repository.ConfigScoped`, which used to return the error. An unreadable system file still fails, as in Git.
  | 
  | ## Testing
  | 
  | Unit tests cover the policy matrix and environment overrides, lookup-time validation of unknown and empty values, config round-trips and scope merging, caller options on submodule updates, a policy set only in the global config for a fetch and a submodule update, unreadable global and system config files through the default loader (including a `Remote.List` that skips an unreadable `~/.gitconfig` and still applies the XDG policy), and redirect hops, including a handshake whose discovery request is redirected. `go test -race` passes for `config`, `plumbing/transport/...`, `plumbing/client` and the root package, apart from tests that need github.com or gitlab.com.

PR body:
  | Supersedes #2160, whose commit is the first one here, rebased onto main with the fixes to it folded in.
  | 
  | go-git did not consult `protocol.allow`, `protocol.<name>.allow`, `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` or `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER`, so a `.gitmodules` entry could make a submodule update fetch over `file://` or any other scheme Git refuses by default. This enforces Git's protocol policy at the transport handshake, as [`transport_check_allowed`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/transport.c#L1037-L1150) does.
  | 
  | ## Changes
  | 
  | - **Policy gate.** `client.Client` and each built-in transport check the request's scheme before handshaking or connecting. Defaults match Git: http, https, git and ssh are `always`, ext is `never`, and file and unknown schemes are `user`. Denial returns `transport.ErrProtocolNotAllowed`. `client.WithProtocolPolicy` and `client.WithUserInitiated` supply the policy inputs.
  | - **Lookup-time validation.** As in Git, an allow value is checked when a transport looks it up, through the new `Config.ProtocolPolicy`, not when the config loads: one bad `[protocol "foo"] allow = bogus` no longer stops `PlainOpen`. An unknown or empty value fails the lookup with Git's "unknown value for config '…'" message. `Protocol.Allow` is a `*string`, nil when unset, so an empty value stays set through marshalling and scope merging.
  | - **Every config scope.** Fetches, pushes and submodule updates read the policy from the repository config merged with the global and system configs when a `ConfigLoader` plugin is registered (the default), as Git reads all three. A global file that cannot be read for lack of permission is skipped, and `~/.gitconfig` then gives way to the XDG file, while an unreadable system file fails the operation, as in [Git](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/config.c#L1541-L1557). Unlike Git, only one global file is read, `~/.gitconfig` or else the XDG one, and `[include]` and `[includeIf]` are not followed.
  | - **Submodules.** Submodule fetches are never user-initiated: `WithUserInitiated(false)` now follows the caller's options, as Git's submodule update sets `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER=0` whatever the caller passes. A caller's `WithProtocolPolicy` still overlays the submodule's policy key by key, like `git -c`.
  | - **Redirects.** Every HTTP redirect hop is checked against the policy as a non-user request, as Git restricts [`CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/http.c#L1148-L1161). This refuses an http to https hop under `protocol.https.allow=never`, and an http to http one under `protocol.http.allow=user`.
  | - **Config round-trips.** Clearing `Protocol.Allow` or a per-scheme entry removes the key on marshal, without dropping `protocol.version`, unrelated keys or the other entries. A config read error fails the operation rather than falling back to the defaults.
  | 
  | ## Behaviour changes
  | 
  | - A `file://` submodule is refused unless `protocol.file.allow` (in any scope) or `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` allows it, as in Git.
  | - A redirect to a protocol the policy forbids for non-user requests fails a handshake that used to follow it.
  | - Fetch, push, `Remote.List` and `ArchiveRemote` now read the host's global and system config on every operation; before, they read no host config at all.
  | - A global or system config with bad syntax now fails them, as it fails Git. A value go-git would refuse elsewhere in those files, such as `[pack] window = x`, does not, since only the protocol policy is interpreted.
  | - The `ConfigLoader` plugin key is frozen at the first such operation, so an embedder must register its loader before it; registering later returns `plugin.ErrFrozen`.
  | - An unreadable global config file (`~/.gitconfig`, the XDG file or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`) is skipped rather than failing the operation, as Git skips it; this also applies to `Repository.ConfigScoped`, which used to return the error. An unreadable system file still fails, as in Git.
  | 
  | ## Testing
  | 
  | Unit tests cover the policy matrix and environment overrides, lookup-time validation of unknown and empty values, config round-trips and scope merging, caller options on submodule updates, a policy set only in the global config for a fetch and a submodule update, unreadable global and system config files through the default loader (including a `Remote.List` that skips an unreadable `~/.gitconfig` and still applies the XDG policy), and redirect hops, including a handshake whose discovery request is redirected. `go test -race` passes for `config`, `plumbing/transport/...`, `plumbing/client` and the root package, apart from tests that need github.com or gitlab.com.

# PR Review: go-git/go-git#2403, "*: Enforce protocol.allow at the transport handshake"

**Reviewed at:** 2026-11-04, follow-up to `2026-11-03-001-REVIEW.md` (head then 527d9792, now ff023847). Steps 9 and 10 of review-pr were skipped as instructed. Nothing was persisted under ~/git/tasks/reviews.

**Summary.** The PR has been squashed into 4 commits on merge-base 500c64d6:
- 60dbf82f is the core gate.
- 01c22180 makes submodule fetches non-user-initiated.
- 2e406ea1 reads the policy from every config scope.
- ff023847 applies the policy to redirect hops.

All eight required changes from the previous consolidated review are addressed. Seven are fully fixed, and each fix has a test that fails when the fix is reverted (mutations below). The eighth, the per-operation config reads, is reduced but by design not eliminated. What is left is minor or a nit, and most of it is documented in COMPATIBILITY.md. **Verdict: approve.** The `file://` submodule default still needs a maintainer's sign-off.

**Is the claimed gap real at the range base? Yes.** At 500c64d6, `git grep -nE 'protocol\.allow|GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL|GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER|ProtocolPolicy|FromUser' 500c64d6 -- '*.go'` returns nothing. The base has no protocol gate, so a `.gitmodules` `file://` URL is fetched without any check.

## How I checked
- **Build, vet and format.** At HEAD, `go build ./...` and `go vet` (config, plumbing/transport/..., plumbing/client, x/plugin/..., root) are clean, and `gofmt -l` reports no changed file.
- **golangci-lint could not run.** Its toolchain (go1.26.5) does not match /usr/bin/go (go1.26.10), so every package failed typecheck.
- **Tests.** `go test -race` passes for `config`, `plumbing/transport`, `plumbing/transport/{http,file,ssh}`, `plumbing/client` and `x/plugin/...`. `go test -count=1 .` (root) passes.
  - `plumbing/transport/git` TestUploadPackSuite fails with "context canceled before the port is connectable".
  - It fails the same way on a `git archive` of the base 500c64d6. It is an environment problem with git-daemon, not this PR.
- **Mutations.** I applied each one to a `git archive HEAD` copy in `$S/tmp/2403-A/src`. The shared worktree was not touched.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Remove `withProtocolGate` from the POST context (handshake.go:597) | `TestFetchRefusesRedirectedPostToUserOnlyProtocol` fails |
| M2 | `overlayPolicy` replaces the config instead of merging it (client.go:256) | `TestHandshake_ProtocolPoliciesOverlayKeyByKey` fails. Root-package tests still pass (R6) |
| M3 | `LoadProtocolPolicy` unmarshals in full | `TestProtocolPolicyIgnoresUnrelatedGlobalConfig` fails |
| M4 | `ArchiveRemote` passes a nil config | `TestProtocolPolicyWithoutRepository` fails |
| M5 | `Remote.repoConfig` returns nil for a storer-less Remote | `TestProtocolPolicyWithoutRepository` fails |
| M6 | Unreadable global files are not skipped | `TestAutoUnreadableGlobal` and `TestRemoteListUnreadableGlobalConfig` fail |
| M7 | `WithUserInitiated(false)` placed before the caller's options | `TestSubmoduleUpdate_CallerOptions` fails |

- **Upstream** (~/git/go-git/git, v2.56.0):
  - config.c:1583-1598. The system file is gentle only for `read_very_early_config` and protected config (config.c:1725, 2465). The normal path dies, so the PR's claim that "an unreadable system file fails" holds.
  - Git reads both the XDG file and `~/.gitconfig`, with `ACCESS_EACCES_OK` (config.c:1592-1598).
  - `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` replaces both (config.c:1539-1544).

## Status of prior findings (2026-11-03-001-REVIEW.md)

| Prior item | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Caller policy replaces the merged config | **Resolved** | `overlayPolicy` uses `config.Merge`, which copies map entries one by one (config.go:316-328) and carries the `*string`. `newClient` prepends the repo policy, so the caller's options overlay it. M2 is caught. |
| 2. `ArchiveRemote` and a storer-less `Remote` ignore global/system | **Resolved** | archive.go:34 and remote.go:77-82 call `policyConfig(nil)`. M4 and M5 are caught. |
| 3. Unrelated global keys (`[pack] window = x`) break fetch | **Resolved** | `plugin.ProtocolPolicySource` and `config.ReadProtocolPolicy` decode only the syntax and the allow keys. M3 is caught. A third-party loader without it still does a full Load, which is documented. |
| 4. Global/system reparsed on every operation | **Partly resolved** | They are no longer read when `NoFetch` is set, and no longer twice in `submoduleClientOptions`. They are still read on every fetch, push and list, which is now stated as intended (R2). |
| 5. No test for the POST-redirect gate | **Resolved** | redirect_protocol_test.go:101. M1 is caught. |
| 6. Duplicate `CheckRequest` in Handshake, `resolve()` removal | **Resolved** | The file/git/ssh `Handshake` no longer check, and `resolve()` is restored, though moved (R5). Through `Client` a request is still checked twice: once by the client and once by the transport's `Connect`. That is reasonable defence in depth for transports used directly. |
| 7. `AllowByName` marshalled in map order | **Resolved** | config.go:1078 uses `slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(...))`. |
| 8. COMPATIBILITY.md on `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER` precedence | **Resolved** | It now reads "unless the caller sets `WithUserInitiated` or `Request.FromUser`". |
| Optional: retitle | **Resolved** | The title is now the first commit's subject. |
| Optional: redundant `WithProtocolPolicy` in `submoduleClientOptions` | **Resolved** | Removed (submodule.go:198-202). |
| Optional: `GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER=1k` rejected | **Still present** | policy.go `parseEnvBool` (R7). This fails closed. |
| Optional: refusal text differs from Git's | Still present | Not re-listed. Cosmetic. |

## Security
- **Minor (R1).** The policy loader does not read every global file Git reads.
  - It reads one global file only: `~/.gitconfig` if it can be read, otherwise the XDG file. It does not follow `[include]` or `[includeIf]`.
  - So a `protocol.file.allow=never` placed in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config` while `~/.gitconfig` exists, or in an included file, is ignored by go-git and enforced by Git (config.c:1592-1598).
  - This is a pre-existing loader limitation, documented in COMPATIBILITY.md. This PR makes it decide a security policy, which fails open relative to Git.
  - The defaults still deny `file://` for submodules, so only an explicit restriction the user added is lost.
- No bypass found:
  - Client-level and transport-level gates cover custom `WithTransport` schemes.
  - Submodule fetches are forced non-user after the caller's options.
  - Redirect hops, GET and POST, are checked as non-user with the session's effective (merged) config.
  - Config read errors fail closed.
  - `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` set but empty denies every scheme.
  - The per-scheme key beats `protocol.allow` across scopes, as in Git's configset lookup.
- No text in the PR body, commits or code addresses reviewers or AI tools.

## Performance
- **Minor (R2).** Every Fetch, Push, List and ArchiveRemote opens and decodes the system and global config files (repository.go:784-808).
  - The orphan-commit refetch in `fetchAndCheckout` (submodule.go:372) reads them a second time per submodule.
  - `Client.Handshake` and `Connect` also do a reflection-based `config.Merge` per request (client.go:256).
  - The cost is small next to network I/O, and Git also rereads config per process.

## Go best practices
- **Nit (R4).** `Remote.repoConfig`'s `if r.s == nil` branch is redundant. A nil `storage.Storer` converts to a nil `config.ConfigStorer`, so `policyConfig(r.s)` already takes the nil path (remote.go:78-80). `policyConfig` without a loader merges two empty configs into `local` (repository.go:787) where a plain copy would do.
- **Nit (R5).** `Client.resolve` is moved unchanged from below `Close` to below `requestWithDefaults` (client.go:361). That is diff noise in a security-sensitive file.
- **Nit (R6).** The root-package "caller over local" case in `TestProtocolPolicyPrecedence` does not detect a replace-instead-of-overlay regression (M2 passes it). Only `plumbing/client` covers key-by-key overlay. A root case would close this, with the caller allowing `file` and the global config denying another scheme the test uses.
- The tests that swap the process-global `ConfigLoader` or use `t.Setenv` are correctly non-parallel and restore the loader with `t.Cleanup(registerTestConfigLoader)`. Sequential top-level tests finish before parallel ones resume, so nothing races.

## Backwards compatibility
- **Minor (R3).** Network operations now depend on host config and on the plugin registry by default. All of this is documented in COMPATIBILITY.md and the PR body.
  - The default `ConfigLoader` (x/plugin/plugin_config.go:11) means every Fetch, Push, List and ArchiveRemote now reads the host's `~/.gitconfig` and `/etc/gitconfig`.
  - A syntactically invalid file, or an unreadable system file, now fails those operations.
  - `plugin.Get` freezes the `ConfigLoader` key on the first such operation (x/plugin/plugin.go:84), so an embedder that registers its loader after a first fetch now gets `ErrFrozen`.
  - Server-side embedders that never expected host config to matter should be warned in release notes.
- `Repository.ConfigScoped` now skips an unreadable global file instead of returning the error. This is documented and matches Git.
- Documented behaviour changes:
  - `file://` submodules are denied by default.
  - Redirects to schemes not allowed for non-user requests fail.
- New exports are additive:
  - `config`: `Protocol.Allow`, `Protocol.AllowByName`, `Config.ProtocolPolicy`, `ReadProtocolPolicy`, `Protocol{Never,User,Always}`.
  - `transport`: `ErrProtocolNotAllowed`, `CheckRequest`, `Request.{FromUser,Config}`.
  - `client`: `WithProtocolPolicy`, `WithUserInitiated`.
  - `plugin`: `ProtocolPolicySource`.

## Blocking issues
None.

## Suggestions
- Read the XDG and `~/.gitconfig` files together for the policy, as Git does, or at least for `LoadProtocolPolicy` (R1).
- Drop the redundant nil branch in `repoConfig` (R4).
- Keep `resolve()` in its original position (R5).
- Add a root-level overlay test (R6).
- Mention the loader freeze and the host-config dependency in release notes (R3).

## Questions for the author
- Is reading only one global file for the policy an accepted gap, or a follow-up? Git honours a `protocol.*.allow` in the XDG file even when `~/.gitconfig` exists.

# go-git#2403 git-conformance review (Agent B)

Range `500c64d6..ff023847` (4 commits) in `~/git/go-git/wt-pr-2403`, compared against upstream Git v2.56.0 at `~/git/go-git/git` and checked with system git 2.56 under an isolated HOME and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`. I built the go-git probe as a separate module under `$S/tmp/2403-B/probe`, with a `replace` that points at the worktree. The worktree was not edited and is clean at `ff023847`.

Tests: `config`, `plumbing/transport`, `transport/http`, `transport/file`, `transport/ssh`, `plumbing/client` and `x/plugin/...` pass. `transport/git` fails here because `git daemon` is not installed on this host ("context canceled before the port is connectable"). That failure comes from the environment, not from the PR.

## Conformant
- **Lookup order and defaults** (`plumbing/transport/policy.go`, `config/protocolpolicy.go`) match `transport.c:1130-1167`. The order is `protocol.<name>.allow`, then `protocol.allow`, then the built-in defaults: http/https/git/ssh always, ext never, everything else user.
- **Value parsing** matches `transport.c:1117-1128`. It is case-insensitive, and it is checked only for the key that is looked up. Git's message text is kept. An empty value fails, and so does a key with no value.
- **`GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL`** overrides every other source, matches case-sensitively, and denies everything when empty (`transport.c:1092-1109`, `1171-1173`).
- **`GIT_PROTOCOL_FROM_USER`** is consulted only in the user tier. An explicit flag wins over it. An unset variable means true and an empty one means false (`transport.c:1180-1183`).

- **Archive and storer-less Remote (prior C2, fixed).** Both now call `policyConfig(nil)` and read the global and system configs, as `git ls-remote` and `git archive --remote` do outside a repository.
- **Lazy validation.** Global and system configs are read through `ReadProtocolPolicy`, which interprets only the protocol keys. As in Git, an unrelated bad value no longer fails a fetch.
- **Redirects.** Every hop, POST included, is checked as not user-initiated against the same merged policy. This matches `CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS` built with `get_curl_allowed_protocols(0)` (`http.c:1228-1244`).
- **Submodules.** `WithUserInitiated(false)` is appended after the caller's options, so it always wins, matching `git-submodule.sh:27-30`. The policy comes from the submodule's own config plus the global and system configs, as for a `git fetch` spawned in the submodule.
- **Marshal (prior C4, map-order part fixed).** New `protocol.<name>` subsections are written in sorted order.

# go-git/go-git#2403 *: Enforce protocol.allow at the transport handshake (@hiddeco)

**Outcome:** changes required
All eight prior required items are fixed and pinned by mutation-tested tests, but the policy still ignores three config sources Git reads (the XDG file next to `~/.gitconfig`, includes, and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`), so a restrictive policy there fails open.

## Required changes
1. [security] Read both global files for the policy, XDG first and then `~/.gitconfig`, and fix the comment that calls them mutually exclusive (x/plugin/config/auto.go:109-116, comment :146-147). With an empty `~/.gitconfig` and `protocol.file.allow=never` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`, git 2.56 refuses `ls-remote` while go-git's `Remote.List` returns 2 refs, so the restriction fails open. Made worse by this PR: the one-file choice predates it, but the PR makes it decide the protocol policy and rewrites the comment. upstream: config.c:1590-1598
2. [security] Follow `[include]` and `[includeIf]` when reading the protocol policy (config/config.go:771-778). A `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` file with `[include] path=<f>` and `protocol.file.allow=never` in `<f>` makes git refuse and go-git list refs. Made worse by this PR: go-git never followed includes, and the PR makes an included policy security-relevant. upstream: config.c:2297-2304 (`opts.respect_includes = 1`)
3. [security] Read `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` last, so they override every file (repository.go:778-804). With `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=never`, as a parent `git -c` passes down, git refuses and go-git lists 2 refs. Made worse by this PR. upstream: config.c:1613
4. [performance] Avoid re-opening and re-decoding the system and global files on every Fetch, Push, List and ArchiveRemote, twice per submodule on the orphan refetch, plus a reflection `config.Merge` per Handshake/Connect (repository.go:784-808, submodule.go:353 and :372, plugmbing/client/client.go:256). The cost scales with operations, not config changes. Introduced by this PR (prior item 4, partly fixed).
5. [conformance] Accept the legacy dotted section syntax that Git parses in global and system files (config/config.go:771-778, propagated at repository.go:795-801). `[protocol.file]\n\tallow = never` makes `ReadProtocolPolicy` fail with `1:10: illegal character U+002E '.'`, which now breaks every fetch, push and list, while git reads it as `protocol.file.allow=never`. The PR body's "as it fails Git" does not hold for this case. Made worse by this PR. upstream: config.c:997
6. [other] Revert the move of `Client.resolve` (plumbing/client/client.go:361-366). Its body is unchanged, so the hunk serves no part of the purpose and adds noise to a security-sensitive file. Introduced by this PR.
7. [other] Drop the `configScoped(s, scope)` extraction or give it a second caller (repository.go:714-720). Only `ConfigScoped` calls it, and `policyConfig` does not use it. Introduced by this PR.
8. [other] Scope the new gentle handling of an unreadable global file (EACCES) and ENOTDIR paths to the policy loader, or justify applying it to the existing `Load`/`ConfigScoped` path (x/plugin/config/auto.go:66-71, :102-118, :224-230). Loading the protocol policy does not need `Repository.ConfigScoped` to stop returning the error. Introduced by this PR.
9. [other] Make the root-package "caller over local" case in `TestProtocolPolicyPrecedence` detect a replace-instead-of-overlay regression (submodule_policy_test.go:388). With `overlayPolicy` replacing the config (`merged := *top`), the root tests still pass, and only `plumbing/client` catches it. Introduced by this PR.

## Optional
- R3: release notes should say network operations now read host global and system config by default, fail on bad syntax or an unreadable system file, and freeze the `ConfigLoader` key on first use (x/plugin/plugin_config.go:44-52, x/plugin/plugin.go:84). **Risk:** low. Main has no protocol gate at all, so the PR only adds a defence. ## Message to contributor
@hiddeco thanks for looking into this. 🙇

Every item from the last round is fixed, and each fix is pinned: making `overlayPolicy` replace the config, passing a nil config from `ArchiveRemote`, dropping the POST redirect gate or putting `WithUserInitiated(false)` before the caller's options all fail a test now. 👏 A few things to fix before merge:
- with an empty `~/.gitconfig` and `protocol.file.allow=never` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`, `git ls-remote` refuses the `file` transport but `Remote.List` returns refs. Git reads the XDG file and then `~/.gitconfig` (config.c:1590-1598), while `auto.go:109-116` stops at the first readable one, and the comment at :146-147 says Git treats them as alternatives.
- a `protocol.file.allow=never` in a file pulled in by `[include] path=...` is enforced by git and ignored by go-git, since `ReadProtocolPolicy` never resolves includes (config/config.go:771). Git reads repo config with `respect_includes` (config.c:2304).
- `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=never`, which is how a parent `git -c` passes config down, makes git refuse and go-git list refs. Git applies these after every file (config.c:1613), and `policyConfig` never reads them (repository.go:778).
- every Fetch, Push, List and ArchiveRemote reopens and decodes the system and global files, a submodule needing the by-hash refetch does it twice (submodule.go:353 and :372), and each Handshake/Connect adds a reflection `config.Merge` (client.go:256). Could the policy be loaded once per operation chain?
- a `~/.gitconfig` with a legacy `[protocol.file]` section now makes every fetch fail with `1:10: illegal character U+002E '.'`, while git reads it as `protocol.file.allow` (config.c:997). So "bad syntax fails them, as it fails Git" in the body does not hold for syntax Git accepts.
- `Client.resolve` is moved below `Connect` with an unchanged body (client.go:361-366). Could it stay where it was?
- `configScoped(s, scope)` is only called by `ConfigScoped` (repository.go:714-720). Could it be folded back in?
- the new EACCES/ENOTDIR skipping in `auto.go` also changes `Load`, so `Repository.ConfigScoped` stops returning an error for an unreadable `~/.gitconfig` (auto.go:66-71, :224-230). Either keep it on the policy path or say in the body why `ConfigScoped` should change too.
- making `overlayPolicy` replace instead of merge (`merged := *top`) still passes the "caller over local" case of `TestProtocolPolicyPrecedence` (submodule_policy_test.go:388). A caller that allows `file` while another scope denies a second scheme the test uses would catch it at the root level.

PR body:
  | Extends #2266 by @Sahana2524 (thank you for your contribution, and sorry about the wait! :bow:)
  | 
  | Builds on #2375, now on main: nonrecursive removal preserves submodule directories without accessing their metadata files, allowing this change to remove the old exception for nested `.git` paths.
  | 
  | ## Summary
  | 
  | Path validation did not consistently account for names that NTFS or HFS+ interprets differently from their spelling. This could let repository paths escape their intended directory or reach Git metadata. This change closes those validation gaps while restoring checkout of ordinary POSIX filenames that were incorrectly subject to Windows restrictions.
  | 
  | ## Behaviour changes
  | 
  | - **Validate paths at filesystem operations as well as tree lookup.** Some paths used by worktree operations do not pass through tree validation, such as the deletions of a reset. Apply the checks there too, at every component, as Git's `verify_path_internal` does [1]: a literal `.` or `..` and `.git` in any case are always refused, and `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` add the `.git` aliases those filesystems fold, the 8.3 short name `git~1` among them. As in Git, tree and worktree paths refuse only the literal `.` and `..`; an NTFS or HFS+ spelling of either is an ordinary name there.
  | - **Apply Windows filename rules on Windows.** POSIX checkouts now accept names such as `aux.c` and filenames ending in a space or period, following Git's platform-specific validation [2]. Windows gains the missing illegal-character and trailing-space/period checks, and `LPT0`, under `core.protectNTFS` [3]; volume-prefix checks apply regardless of that setting. NTFS metadata protection remains available on every host because a process can access NTFS from another operating system.
  | - **Protect `.git` aliases throughout worktree paths.** The worktree filesystem refuses `.git` and its aliases at every position. `Status` and `Clean` list the worktree directly and skip only `.git`, so an untracked alias such as `git~1` is listed file by file and removed by `Clean`, as `git clean -fd` does [4]. Adding an alias fails with `ErrInvalidPath`, as `git add` fails with "invalid path".
  | - **Validate submodule paths before they are chrooted into.** `Submodule.Repository` and the `.gitmodules` parser check the path with `pathutil.ValidSubmodulePath`, which is `ValidTreePath` plus the NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..`; such a component would scope the submodule worktree to the superproject root. `DotGit.Module` checks the storage name with `pathutil.ValidStorageName`, as the parser does, rather than relying on `path.Clean`.
  | 
  | ## Compatibility
  | 
  | - **Submodule paths and names have stricter rules than Git.** The NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..` are refused in submodule paths and storage names on every host, whatever `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` say. This is deliberate go-git policy: Git's `check_submodule_name` refuses only an empty name and a literal `..` [5], and Git does not validate the `.gitmodules` path at all. Storage names also refuse a NUL, a leading or trailing separator and a drive prefix. A run of periods, such as `...`, stays valid, as in Git, and ordinary tree paths keep the folded spellings so valid POSIX repositories remain readable.
  | - **Portable checks can reject names Git accepts locally.** go-git treats both slash styles as separators on every host. On Windows, `DotGit.Module` refuses a storage name that is not a valid Win32 path without consulting `core.protectNTFS`, which `DotGit` cannot read; Git's check accepts any name with that setting off [6].
  | - **`.git` is skipped in any case.** `Status` and `Clean` skip `.git` case-insensitively whatever `core.ignorecase` says, where Git does so only under that setting [4]. This is deliberate: on a case-insensitive filesystem `.GIT` may be the repository's own directory, which would otherwise be listed and removed by `Clean`. On a case-sensitive filesystem without `core.ignorecase`, an untracked `.GIT` that Git lists is not reported.
  | - **Unsafe submodule paths take precedence over missing fields.** Parsing `.gitmodules` discards such entries, and those with a `.git` alias or a control byte in the path, rather than retaining them as incomplete configuration. Filesystem module storage also validates names supplied directly by callers.
  | 
  | General nested-repository handling in `Clean` remains a separate issue; a directory preserved by reset can still be affected by a later clean.
  |

  | [2]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/git-compat-util.h#L154-L164
  | [3]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/compat/mingw.c#L3347-L3469

  | Extends #2266 by @Sahana2524 (thank you for your contribution, and sorry about the wait! :bow:)
  | 
  | Builds on #2375, now on main: nonrecursive removal preserves submodule directories without accessing their metadata files, allowing this change to remove the old exception for nested `.git` paths.
  | 
  | ## Summary
  | 
  | Path validation did not consistently account for names that NTFS or HFS+ interprets differently from their spelling. This could let repository paths escape their intended directory or reach Git metadata. This change closes those validation gaps while restoring checkout of ordinary POSIX filenames that were incorrectly subject to Windows restrictions.
  | 
  | ## Behaviour changes
  | 
  | - **Validate paths at filesystem operations as well as tree lookup.** Some paths used by worktree operations do not pass through tree validation, such as the deletions of a reset. Apply the checks there too, at every component, as Git's `verify_path_internal` does [1]: a literal `.` or `..` and `.git` in any case are always refused, and `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` add the `.git` aliases those filesystems fold, the 8.3 short name `git~1` among them. As in Git, tree and worktree paths refuse only the literal `.` and `..`; an NTFS or HFS+ spelling of either is an ordinary name there.
  | - **Apply Windows filename rules on Windows.** POSIX checkouts now accept names such as `aux.c` and filenames ending in a space or period, following Git's platform-specific validation [2]. Windows gains the missing illegal-character and trailing-space/period checks, and `LPT0`, under `core.protectNTFS` [3]; volume-prefix checks apply regardless of that setting. NTFS metadata protection remains available on every host because a process can access NTFS from another operating system.
  | - **Protect `.git` aliases throughout worktree paths.** The worktree filesystem refuses `.git` and its aliases at every position. `Status` and `Clean` list the worktree directly and skip only `.git`, so an untracked alias such as `git~1` is listed file by file and removed by `Clean`, as `git clean -fd` does [4]. Adding an alias fails with `ErrInvalidPath`, as `git add` fails with "invalid path".
  | - **Validate submodule paths before they are chrooted into.** `Submodule.Repository` and the `.gitmodules` parser check the path with `pathutil.ValidSubmodulePath`, which is `ValidTreePath` plus the NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..`; such a component would scope the submodule worktree to the superproject root. `DotGit.Module` checks the storage name with `pathutil.ValidStorageName`, as the parser does, rather than relying on `path.Clean`.
  | 
  | ## Compatibility
  | 
  | - **Submodule paths and names have stricter rules than Git.** The NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..` are refused in submodule paths and storage names on every host, whatever `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` say. This is deliberate go-git policy: Git's `check_submodule_name` refuses only an empty name and a literal `..` [5], and Git does not validate the `.gitmodules` path at all. Storage names also refuse a NUL, a leading or trailing separator and a drive prefix. A run of periods, such as `...`, stays valid, as in Git, and ordinary tree paths keep the folded spellings so valid POSIX repositories remain readable.
  | - **Portable checks can reject names Git accepts locally.** go-git treats both slash styles as separators on every host. On Windows, `DotGit.Module` refuses a storage name that is not a valid Win32 path without consulting `core.protectNTFS`, which `DotGit` cannot read; Git's check accepts any name with that setting off [6].
  | - **`.git` is skipped in any case.** `Status` and `Clean` skip `.git` case-insensitively whatever `core.ignorecase` says, where Git does so only under that setting [4]. This is deliberate: on a case-insensitive filesystem `.GIT` may be the repository's own directory, which would otherwise be listed and removed by `Clean`. On a case-sensitive filesystem without `core.ignorecase`, an untracked `.GIT` that Git lists is not reported.
  | - **Unsafe submodule paths take precedence over missing fields.** Parsing `.gitmodules` discards such entries, and those with a `.git` alias or a control byte in the path, rather than retaining them as incomplete configuration. Filesystem module storage also validates names supplied directly by callers.
  | 
  | General nested-repository handling in `Clean` remains a separate issue; a directory preserved by reset can still be affected by a later clean.

10	  | Extends #2266 by @Sahana2524 (thank you for your contribution, and sorry about the wait! :bow:)
11	  | 
12	  | Builds on #2375, now on main: nonrecursive removal preserves submodule directories without accessing their metadata files, allowing this change to remove the old exception for nested `.git` paths.
13	  | 
14	  | ## Summary
15	  | 
16	  | Path validation did not consistently account for names that NTFS or HFS+ interprets differently from their spelling. This could let repository paths escape their intended directory or reach Git metadata. This change closes those validation gaps while restoring checkout of ordinary POSIX filenames that were incorrectly subject to Windows restrictions.
17	  | 
18	  | ## Behaviour changes
19	  | 
20	  | - **Validate paths at filesystem operations as well as tree lookup.** Some paths used by worktree operations do not pass through tree validation, such as the deletions of a reset. Apply the checks there too, at every component, as Git's `verify_path_internal` does [1]: a literal `.` or `..` and `.git` in any case are always refused, and `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` add the `.git` aliases those filesystems fold, the 8.3 short name `git~1` among them. As in Git, tree and worktree paths refuse only the literal `.` and `..`; an NTFS or HFS+ spelling of either is an ordinary name there.
21	  | - **Apply Windows filename rules on Windows.** POSIX checkouts now accept names such as `aux.c` and filenames ending in a space or period, following Git's platform-specific validation [2]. Windows gains the missing illegal-character and trailing-space/period checks, and `LPT0`, under `core.protectNTFS` [3]; volume-prefix checks apply regardless of that setting. NTFS metadata protection remains available on every host because a process can access NTFS from another operating system.
22	  | - **Protect `.git` aliases throughout worktree paths.** The worktree filesystem refuses `.git` and its aliases at every position. `Status` and `Clean` list the worktree directly and skip only `.git`, so an untracked alias such as `git~1` is listed file by file and removed by `Clean`, as `git clean -fd` does [4]. Adding an alias fails with `ErrInvalidPath`, as `git add` fails with "invalid path".
23	  | - **Validate submodule paths before they are chrooted into.** `Submodule.Repository` and the `.gitmodules` parser check the path with `pathutil.ValidSubmodulePath`, which is `ValidTreePath` plus the NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..`; such a component would scope the submodule worktree to the superproject root. `DotGit.Module` checks the storage name with `pathutil.ValidStorageName`, as the parser does, rather than relying on `path.Clean`.
24	  | 
25	  | ## Compatibility
26	  | 
27	  | - **Submodule paths and names have stricter rules than Git.** The NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..` are refused in submodule paths and storage names on every host, whatever `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` say. This is deliberate go-git policy: Git's `check_submodule_name` refuses only an empty name and a literal `..` [5], and Git does not validate the `.gitmodules` path at all. Storage names also refuse a NUL, a leading or trailing separator and a drive prefix. A run of periods, such as `...`, stays valid, as in Git, and ordinary tree paths keep the folded spellings so valid POSIX repositories remain readable.
28	  | - **Portable checks can reject names Git accepts locally.** go-git treats both slash styles as separators on every host. On Windows, `DotGit.Module` refuses a storage name that is not a valid Win32 path without consulting `core.protectNTFS`, which `DotGit` cannot read; Git's check accepts any name with that setting off [6].
29	  | - **`.git` is skipped in any case.** `Status` and `Clean` skip `.git` case-insensitively whatever `core.ignorecase` says, where Git does so only under that setting [4]. This is deliberate: on a case-insensitive filesystem `.GIT` may be the repository's own directory, which would otherwise be listed and removed by `Clean`. On a case-sensitive filesystem without `core.ignorecase`, an untracked `.GIT` that Git lists is not reported.
30	  | - **Unsafe submodule paths take precedence over missing fields.** Parsing `.gitmodules` discards such entries, and those with a `.git` alias or a control byte in the path, rather than retaining them as incomplete configuration. Filesystem module storage also validates names supplied directly by callers.
31	  | 
32	  | General nested-repository handling in `Clean` remains a separate issue; a directory preserved by reset can still be affected by a later clean.

PR body:
  | Extends #2266 by @Sahana2524 (thank you for your contribution, and sorry about the wait! :bow:)
  | 
  | Builds on #2375, now on main: nonrecursive removal preserves submodule directories without accessing their metadata files, allowing this change to remove the old exception for nested `.git` paths.
  | 
  | ## Summary
  | 
  | Path validation did not consistently account for names that NTFS or HFS+ interprets differently from their spelling. This could let repository paths escape their intended directory or reach Git metadata. This change closes those validation gaps while restoring checkout of ordinary POSIX filenames that were incorrectly subject to Windows restrictions.
  | 
  | ## Behaviour changes
  | 
  | - **Validate paths at filesystem operations as well as tree lookup.** Some paths used by worktree operations do not pass through tree validation, such as the deletions of a reset. Apply the checks there too, at every component, as Git's `verify_path_internal` does [1]: a literal `.` or `..` and `.git` in any case are always refused, and `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` add the `.git` aliases those filesystems fold, the 8.3 short name `git~1` among them. As in Git, tree and worktree paths refuse only the literal `.` and `..`; an NTFS or HFS+ spelling of either is an ordinary name there.
  | - **Apply Windows filename rules on Windows.** POSIX checkouts now accept names such as `aux.c` and filenames ending in a space or period, following Git's platform-specific validation [2]. Windows gains the missing illegal-character and trailing-space/period checks, and `LPT0`, under `core.protectNTFS` [3]; volume-prefix checks apply regardless of that setting. NTFS metadata protection remains available on every host because a process can access NTFS from another operating system.
  | - **Protect `.git` aliases throughout worktree paths.** The worktree filesystem refuses `.git` and its aliases at every position. `Status` and `Clean` list the worktree directly and skip only `.git`, so an untracked alias such as `git~1` is listed file by file and removed by `Clean`, as `git clean -fd` does [4]. Adding an alias fails with `ErrInvalidPath`, as `git add` fails with "invalid path".
  | - **Validate submodule paths before they are chrooted into.** `Submodule.Repository` and the `.gitmodules` parser check the path with `pathutil.ValidSubmodulePath`, which is `ValidTreePath` plus the NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..`; such a component would scope the submodule worktree to the superproject root. `DotGit.Module` checks the storage name with `pathutil.ValidStorageName`, as the parser does, rather than relying on `path.Clean`.
  | 
  | ## Compatibility
  | 
  | - **Submodule paths and names have stricter rules than Git.** The NTFS and HFS+ spellings of `.` and `..` are refused in submodule paths and storage names on every host, whatever `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` say. This is deliberate go-git policy: Git's `check_submodule_name` refuses only an empty name and a literal `..` [5], and Git does not validate the `.gitmodules` path at all. Storage names also refuse a NUL, a leading or trailing separator and a drive prefix. A run of periods, such as `...`, stays valid, as in Git, and ordinary tree paths keep the folded spellings so valid POSIX repositories remain readable.
  | - **Portable checks can reject names Git accepts locally.** go-git treats both slash styles as separators on every host. On Windows, `DotGit.Module` refuses a storage name that is not a valid Win32 path without consulting `core.protectNTFS`, which `DotGit` cannot read; Git's check accepts any name with that setting off [6].
  | - **`.git` is skipped in any case.** `Status` and `Clean` skip `.git` case-insensitively whatever `core.ignorecase` says, where Git does so only under that setting [4]. This is deliberate: on a case-insensitive filesystem `.GIT` may be the repository's own directory, which would otherwise be listed and removed by `Clean`. On a case-sensitive filesystem without `core.ignorecase`, an untracked `.GIT` that Git lists is not reported.
  | - **Unsafe submodule paths take precedence over missing fields.** Parsing `.gitmodules` discards such entries, and those with a `.git` alias or a control byte in the path, rather than retaining them as incomplete configuration. Filesystem module storage also validates names supplied directly by callers.
  | 
  | General nested-repository handling in `Clean` remains a separate issue; a directory preserved by reset can still be affected by a later clean.
  | 
  | [1]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/read-cache.c#L987-L1048
  | [2]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/git-compat-util.h#L154-L164
  | [3]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/compat/mingw.c#L3347-L3469
  | [4]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/dir.c#L2439
  | [5]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/submodule-config.c#L214-L237
  | [6]: https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/compat/mingw.c#L3347-L3353

# PR Review: go-git/go-git#2376 — *: Fix path validation across storage and worktree operations

**Reviewed at:** 2026-11-04, iteration 008 (Agent A, review-pr). Previous review: `2026-11-03-001-REVIEW.md`, at head `ccad2db6`.

**Summary:** The PR has been squashed from 15 commits into 3 (`791731a2`, `e43c13e5`, `2b34ce5d`) on base `500c64d6`. The design changed:
- `ValidTreePath` and `validPath` now refuse only a literal `.` or `..`.
- The folded spellings of `.` and `..` move to the new `ValidSubmodulePath` and `ValidStorageName`, which only submodule code uses.
- The `git~1` and NTFS/HFS `.git` aliases in `validPath` are now gated on `core.protectNTFS` and `core.protectHFS`. A case-insensitive `.git` is refused at every position.
- `Status` and `Clean` now go straight to the underlying billy filesystem and skip `.git` in any case. The `Options.Opaque` hook is gone.

All seven required items from the last review are resolved. The main new problem is a merge break. Main gained two 3-argument `gitAtLeast` callers after this base, and the PR changes `gitAtLeast` to take 4 arguments. So the merge fails to compile even after the textual conflict in `worktree_status_test.go` is resolved. Verdict: **approve after rebase**, plus minor items.

**Verification:**
- Tests ran on a `git archive` copy of `2b34ce5d`, Linux, go1.26.10, git 2.56.0.
- `go vet ./...` is clean. `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=darwin` vet are clean on `.`, `internal/pathutil`, `dotgit` and `config`.
- `go test` passes for `.` (50s), `internal/pathutil`, `config`, `storage/filesystem/dotgit`, `utils/merkletrie/...` and `plumbing/object`.
- I did not run anything on Windows or HFS+.
- The shared worktree was not modified.

## Are the claimed bugs real at the range base (500c64d6)?

These are probe results, base then head:

| Probe | Base 500c64d6 | Head 2b34ce5d |
|---|---|---|
| `Create("aux.c")`, protect on, POSIX | `invalid path` (**real bug**, #2322) | ok |
| `Create("sub/.git")`, `sub/.GIT`, `sub/git~1` | accepted (final position tolerated) | refused |
| `Create("git~1")`, protect off | refused (unconditional) | accepted (matches Git) |
| `DotGit.Module("")` / `("/")` | root `/modules`, nil error (**real**) | `ErrModuleNameEscape` |
| `Module(". ")`, `("a\x00b")`, `("C:x")` | accepted | refused |
| `Module("...")` | accepted | accepted (as Git) |
| `Status` with untracked `git~1/f` or `dir/.git /x` | `readdir: invalid path` error (**real**) | succeeds, lists file by file |
| `Clean` with untracked `dir/git~1/f` | `remove: invalid path component`, leaves it and `z` (**real**) | removes both |

The submodule chroot escape through `.. ` or `.<U+200C>.` depends on how Windows or HFS+ resolves those names. It is not exploitable on POSIX, and I have not reproduced it on the affected filesystems. The PR describes it accurately as filesystem-dependent.

# 2376-B: git-conformance, go-git/go-git#2376 range 500c64d6..2b34ce5d (3 commits)

Upstream: ~/git/go-git/git, read at tag v2.54.0 (the PR's citations) with git 2.56.0 for live comparison.
Method: `git archive` copies of head and base under $S/tmp/2376-B (shared worktree untouched, still clean at 2b34ce5d). Probe tests on validPath (all 4 protect combinations), ValidTreePath, ValidSubmodulePath, ValidStorageName, and Status/Clean on a real osfs repo; same tree run through `git status --porcelain -uall`, `git clean -fdn` and `git update-index --cacheinfo`. ## Risk: low

The PR is mostly a tightening. The places where it gets looser all match upstream and none of them is reachable from a cloned tree:
- `git~1` is now refused by `validPath` only under `core.protectNTFS`.
- Windows reserved names are now accepted on POSIX.
- Periods-only submodule names such as `...` are now accepted.

`ValidTreePath` is unchanged apart from comments. It still refuses `.git`, `git~1` and their NTFS and HFS+ aliases at every position, whatever the settings. I mutated each new gate in turn and a test caught every one, except doClean's case-insensitive `.git` skip (A8). The one real defence-in-depth loss is that `Clean` now deletes through the raw billy filesystem, so the wrapper's leading-symlink check no longer applies (A1). The paths come from a non-following directory listing, so an attacker would have to win a local race. That is not an abuse path a repository can trigger.

- **Each hunk in e43c13e5 is required by the stated purpose:**
  - `Validate`: the path is checked before the URL.
  - `ValidSubmodulePath` is used in place of the regexp.
  - `validSubmoduleName` now delegates to `ValidStorageName`, which also removes the now-dead `regexp`, `strings` and `isPathSep`.
  - `Submodule.Repository` uses `ValidSubmodulePath`.
  - The tests cover the above.
- **The claimed bugs reproduce at the base.** I probed the base parser:
  - `path = ..` with no url is kept (kept=1).
  - `path = a/.git/b` is kept.
  - `Validate` accepts `. `, `.‌`, `.‌.`, `..::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`, `x/.git` and `git~1`.
  - The head refuses all of these.

- **Prior A2** (U+2022 in title): resolved (meta.json title is ASCII).
- **Prior A3** (`build:` prefix): resolved (that commit is gone).
- **Prior A4** (merge hazards): partly resolved. #2384 is clean now. #2372, #2550 and #2551 still conflict (A4).
- **Prior A5** (reserved names off Windows): still present, deliberate, matches upstream.

1. [security] Bound the nesting walk: stop once a prefix directory does not exist (and treat a name-too-long error the same), build prefixes by slicing `cleaned` instead of calling `Join`, and add a deep-name test (dotgit.go:1788-1792). Introduced.

3. [security] In the `..` walk, an `Lstat` error other than not-exist is treated as "not a symlink", so `..` is applied lexically. Git's realpath dies there (dotgit.go:1966-1970 vs setup.c:337). Introduced.
4. [conformance] Run the walk on the uncleaned `modules/<name>`, after the escape check, or reject `.` components in submodule names. Today `a/.` is accepted after `a` is initialised, and the two share `modules/a` (dotgit.go:1766-1772). Real `git clone --recurse-submodules` refuses with "submodule git dir '.../modules/a/.' is inside git dir '.../modules/a'". `config/modules.go:143` lets `a/.` through.
5. [conformance] Use `Lstat` for `commondir` and treat an existing entry that can't be read as an error (dotgit.go:1825). Introduced (nit). Upstream `file_exists` uses lstat (dir.c:3191-3195) and dies on a failed read (setup.c:328-329). A dangling symlink currently counts as "no commondir". This needs local `.git` write access to hit.
6. [other] Rebase onto main fc38df4d. The conflict is one hunk in the top `const` block (dotgit.go:71) against #2401's `refLockSuffix`/`maxRefComponentLen`/`maxRefLeafLen`. Keeping both groups merges cleanly and passes `go test -race ./storage/... .`.

  | Directory detection handles symbolic and detached `HEAD` formats and resolves `objects` and `refs` through `commondir`, using the supplied filesystem. The check runs on each resolution, so its result reflects the repositories currently initialized on disk.

A `commondir` that is a symlink to nothing, or whose path has a component that cannot be examined, is reported as an error, as Git fails on both, and errors quote long paths elided.

# PR Review: go-git/go-git#2384, storage: filesystem/dotgit, Reject nested submodule Git directories

**Reviewed at:** 2026-11-04, iteration 002 of this batch. Previous: `2026-11-03-001-REVIEW.md` (head 3c12ce60).
**Range:** 2b34ce5d..b44afee6 (20 commits). This PR is stacked on #2376 (base fix/worktree-path-policy).

**Summary:** Since the last review the PR was rebased onto #2376, and six commits were added:
- 83a17bdc refuses a commondir that goes through a missing directory.
- 466b7982 bounds the quoted path in commondir file errors.
- 3f3ea374 caps a name at 255 components.
- 79402ea9 follows a commondir symlink whose target does not exist.
- e32b79b2 counts a commondir that names a file as "not a Git dir".
- b44afee6 keeps an absolute commondir as written on Windows.

Every required change from the prior review is resolved. One residual remains. The depth cap counts components, not bytes, so on a memfs-backed storage, repeat access still costs seconds per call when the components are long. Verdict: approve, with a minor follow-up.

**Is the claimed bug real at the range base?** Yes. At 2b34ce5d, `Module` runs the name checks and then `Chroot`, and there is no nesting walk. I disabled the `checkModuleGitDirNesting` call in a scratch copy, which reproduces the base. `TestModuleRejectsNestingInsideSiblingGitDir` then fails for `lib/refs/heads`, `lib/packed-refs`, `lib/refs` and `lib/modules/x`, and `TestModuleRejectsNestingOnceOuterModuleExists` fails too.

## Status of prior findings
1. **`..` bypass, `x/../lib/hooks` (required 1): resolved.** The #2376 base now calls `pathutil.ValidStorageName` first, which refuses `.` and `..` components separated by either slash. The test now asserts `ErrModuleNameEscape` for `lib/.`, `lib/./refs` and `x/../lib/hooks` (dotgit_test.go:141-152). This depends on #2376 landing first.
2. **Repeat-access cost (required 2): partly resolved (R1).** `maxModuleNameDepth = 255` (dotgit.go:1919, 1971) bounds the number of components, and `TestModuleRejectsDeepName` runs `Module` again after `Init`. On osfs, PATH_MAX keeps a call at the cap to about 35-40 ms. On memfs the component length has no bound, so the cost per call still grows with the bytes in the name (R1).
3. **commondir with a missing intermediate component (required 3): resolved.** On memfs, a commondir of `missing/deeper` or `missing/../nothere` now returns `submodule common directory "missing/deeper": invalid path "modules/lib/missing"`. A plain `nothere` is still accepted, as Git's realpath accepts a missing last component.
4. **Unelided `commonFile` in errors (required 4): resolved.** Every `read %q` and mode error now uses `elide(commonFile)` and `pathErrCause(err)` (dotgit.go:2044-2078). `TestModuleNestingCommonDirFileErrorQuotesBoundedPath` covers this.
- **Commit subject ending in a period: resolved.** It is now 908e9bd6, "Resolve a common directory the way Git does", without the period.
- **Optional, regular-file check and Open as separate calls (FIFO swap): still present** (dotgit.go:2044/2060, and the same for HEAD). This is a nit that needs local write access.
- **Optional, conflict with #2376: no longer applicable.** The PR is now stacked on #2376 and keeps its pre-checks.

## Security
- **Minor (R1), dotgit.go:1971 and dotgit.go:2004.** The depth cap bounds the number of components but not their length. On memfs (`filesystem.NewStorage(memfs)`), each prefix is still resolved from the root, so the cost of a call scales with (components x bytes). I measured `Module(name)` after `MkdirAll("modules/"+name)` with 255 components, averaged over 10 calls:

  | Filesystem | 1-byte segments | 255-byte segments | 4000-byte segments |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | memfs | 48 ms | 2.7 s | 35.5 s |
  | osfs | 35 ms (PATH_MAX caps the length) | | |

  - The config parser sets no length limit on a name (config/modules.go:136, `ValidStorageName` only). So a hostile `.gitmodules` on a memfs-backed filesystem storage still makes every `Status`/`Update` call slow.
  - A byte cap on `modules/<name>` closes it. For example, 4096 bytes would match PATH_MAX, alongside or instead of the component cap.
  - This sits below the prior required change because OS filesystems are bounded.
  - Introduced: yes (the base has no walk).

## Performance
- R1 is the only finding. Separator-free names do no probing, and an ordinary `deps/foo` costs one Stat plus one Lstat.

## Go best practices
- **Nit (R2), dotgit.go:2044 and dotgit.go:2060.** The `Lstat` mode check and the `Open` of `commondir` (and of `HEAD` in `validHeadRef`) are separate calls. A file swapped locally for a FIFO between the two blocks the reader. This needs local write access. Prior: still present.

All four review files are written and each PR's SUMMARY.md is updated. All four come out as changes required.

| PR | Outcome | Risk | Required items | Review file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| go-git 2472 | changes required | low (codex: none) | 2 | `~/git/tasks/reviews/go-git/go-git/2472/2026-11-04-001-REVIEW.md` |
| go-git 2403 | changes required | low (codex: low) | 9 | `~/git/tasks/reviews/go-git/go-git/2403/2026-11-04-001-REVIEW.md` |
| go-git 2384 | changes required | low (codex: low) | 3 | `~/git/tasks/reviews/go-git/go-git/2384/2026-11-04-001-REVIEW.md` |
| go-git 2376 | changes required | low (codex: low) | 8 | `~/git/tasks/reviews/go-git/go-git/2376/2026-11-04-001-REVIEW.md` |

The required items, in brief:
- **2472:** 2 other items, both nits: no v0/v1 test for the new walker, and a stale-named test that duplicates an existing one. Codex would approve; I kept the lead's outcome.
- **2403:** 3 security, 1 performance, 1 conformance, 4 other.
  - Security: the protocol policy ignores the XDG config file when `~/.gitconfig` exists, `include`/`includeIf`, and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`. A restriction set in any of these fails open compared with git.
  - Performance: system and global config are re-parsed on every operation.
  - Conformance: legacy dotted section syntax like `[protocol.file]` now breaks every fetch, though git accepts it.
  - Other: the `resolve()` move, the `configScoped` extraction, the unreadable-global-file skip also changing `Load`/`ConfigScoped` (codex's third unjustified hunk), and a weak root-level overlay test.
- **2384:** 1 security, 1 performance, 1 other.
  - Security: a `Stat` error on `objects`/`refs` when there is no commondir is treated as "not a git dir", so nesting is accepted.
  - Performance: the 255-component cap doesn't limit bytes, so on memfs one call can take 35.5 s. Codex rates this major.
  - Other: the PR body doesn't mention the cap or `ErrModuleNameTooDeep`.
- **2376:** 1 security, 2 conformance, 5 other.
  - Security: `Clean` no longer runs the leading-symlink check.
  - Conformance: `.git` in any letter case is skipped whatever `core.ignorecase` says, and `DotGit.Module` applies Win32 rules even with `core.protectNTFS=false`.
  - Other: the `gitAtLeast` signature change plus the conflict in `worktree_status_test.go` means the merge with main won't compile. The rest are the BSD licence text in `volume.go`, `ErrModuleNameEscape` returned for names that don't escape, a stale test comment, and Sahana's missing Signed-off-by on 791731a2.

Things worth knowing before you use the files:
- **Dependencies:** the reports record that 2384 depends on 2376 landing first, and that 2472 is stacked on 2477.
- **Severity tags:** `decisions.md` grouped 2403's C1–C3 as "[security/conformance]". I tagged them `[security]` and still cite the upstream file:line for each.
- **Extra edits beyond the brief:** I corrected the stale titles in the 2472 and 2403 SUMMARY headers. In 2376 and 2384, I moved older carried concerns into Resolved where today's raw reports or the worktree confirm them fixed. For 2376 I checked that `errLeadingSymlink` is present at the head, and that `rmEntryAndDirsIfEmpty` and `IsUnsafeStorageName` are gone.
- **What I didn't touch:** no worktrees, no tests run, nothing posted. The messages to the contributor contain no em dashes or semicolons.
